questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.learningObjective: Determine the adiabatic index of a monatomic ideal gas
questions.stem: A field survey tags a sample of monatomic ideal gas and asks for its adiabatic index, defined as the ratio of the two heat capacities.
questions.explanation: For a monatomic gas Cp = (5/2)R and Cv = (3/2)R, so the adiabatic index is 5/3 = 1.6667. The index depends only on the degrees of freedom, not on the temperature or the amount of gas.
questions.hint: The index is the ratio Cp over Cv.

questions.stem: Why is the change in internal energy between two states of an ideal gas the same whatever path connects them?

options.text: Because the internal energy of an ideal gas is stored in intermolecular bonds that never break
options.misconception: credits the internal energy to intermolecular bonds

options.text: Because internal energy is a state function, fixed for a given temperature of the sample
Because the work done along the path is the same whether the path is slow or fast
options.misconception: attributes path independence to the speed of the process

options.text: Because the heat added along the path equals the internal energy change on every path
options.misconception: treats the heat along a path as path independent

questions.explanation: Internal energy is a state function, so its change depends only on the initial and final temperatures. The heat and work along the path differ, but they always sum to the same change.
questions.hint: Ask what kind of quantity internal energy is.

questions.stem: A survey asks for the work done, in joules, when 0.250 mol of gas expands isothermally at 400 K from 0.0100 m3 to 0.0200 m3.
